newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Heineken 96 net seen hit by weather, costs.
newsitem.headline: Heineken 96 net seen hit by weather, costs.

text.p: Last year's cool summer and increased raw material costs are expected to be the main factors behind a forecast 2.5 percent drop in 1996 net profit to some 647 million guilders at Dutch brewer Heineken, analysts said.
Profit forecasts ranged from 630 to 660 million guilders. Heineken will announce its 1996 data on Friday.
"Malt prices were sharply higher and packaging costs rose quite a lot in 1996, but I expect that to improve this year," said ING Barings analyst Gerard Rijk.
Marketing costs as a percentage of sales were also on the rise, said Darrell Duthie, an analyst at MeesPierson.
"Heineken has said it has to spend more and more in order to preserve its market share in a number of countries," he said.

Regional problems in Africa, where some of Heineken's local breweries were working at reduced capacity, would have a limited impact on operating results, analysts said, pencilling in charges of between ten and some tens of millions guilders.
Duthie said Heineken's Italian and French acquisitions had contributed to sales growth in 1996, but added he expected them to be still loss-making.
Analysts were waiting for news on how restructurings in the two countries were working out.
Rijk said he expected Heineken to start reaping benefits in the course of 1997. "Notably in France, Heineken can't reorganise agressively, but must do it step by step, very carefully," he said.
Developments in Asia did not look too bright either, analysts said, as cut-throat competition was pressuring margins.
"Although this will have been partly offset by the higher local dollar," Duthie said.
The higher dollar was seen having a positive impact on results in the second half, as it continued to strengthen after Heineken tempered profit growth expectations last September.
"The dollar's rise since those statements has had a huge impact on results and it will carry on in 1997," said ABN AMRO's analyst David Kerstens.
He said currency factors had caused him to raise 1997 earnings per share estimates by 1.05 guilders to 14.75.
Contrary to profit, sales are expected to increase on 1995's 10.4 billion guilders.

"Overall, I expect a nice growth in 1996 turnover, due not only to acquisitions, but also to relatively healthy organic growth," Duthie said. He expected increased sales in all regions except for Africa and the Netherlands.
"What counts most, is Heineken's view on the future. 1996 is behind us now, and we know more or less it was not brilliant", Duthie said.
Rijk added Heineken did not usually give a concrete forecast on profits for the rest of the year at this early stage.
"But (CEO Karel) Vuursteen will give us his view on the beer markets as a whole, which will be very interesting," Rijk said.
